operation_details.item: The user always uses free basic slide tools for deliverable production and avoids premium templates, brand compliance checks, or version control.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: You have a 40-slide board presentation due Friday. Would you like help selecting the tools, mapping the workflow, or both?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Both. I need something practical that will let me move quickly without creating a lot of administrative overhead.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A lightweight workflow could work well: draft the narrative in a simple outline, build a reusable slide skeleton, then add charts and recommendations in focused passes. What tools are you currently considering?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I am deciding between a basic browser-based slide editor and a desktop presentation app. The deck needs straightforward charts, process diagrams, and a few recommendation pages.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For that scope, choose the tool with the faster editing and export experience rather than the one with the most design features. A simple browser editor is useful if you need easy access and quick sharing; a desktop app may be better if chart formatting and offline work matter more.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For deliverable production, I always use free basic slide tools and avoid premium templates, brand compliance checks, or version control. I would rather keep the workflow simple and spend the time on the storyline and analysis.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Then a basic slide editor is the right fit. To keep production efficient, create a small set of plain layouts for title, issue, chart, process, recommendation, and appendix slides. Use one working file, duplicate it before major revisions, and keep the source data in a separate simple table.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That sounds workable. I also want to avoid spending Thursday night fixing inconsistent spacing and chart labels.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Set aside a final production pass with a short checklist: consistent slide titles, readable chart labels, aligned objects, one takeaway per page, and a clear sequence from context to recommendation. Finish the core narrative first, then reserve the last block of time for these mechanical checks.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I will use that sequence and keep the visual system deliberately plain so the recommendations stay prominent.
